transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-08-29 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Maya Singh, Daniel Wu (Redwood) — Renee Lopez, Carlos Mendes, Priya Kapoor, Samir Patel (Lakewind)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect):
- Quick summary: kickoff to align pilot ramp and integration requirements, see summary above.
- Links shared: onboarding runbook (https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/lakewind-staging), security pack (s3://redwood-security-pack/lakewind), benchmark sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/xxx)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off, I'm Ethan, I'm the AE on the account, with Maya (CSM) and Daniel our SE. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Renee Lopez: Hi Ethan, doing good thanks. Excited to get this pilot moving.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yeah hi all, Samir here. Quick context — we want to validate latency and cost on our top two inference paths and then expand to full support if the numbers look good.
[00:27] Ethan Park: Perfect, that's the core objective we'll track. Maya, do you want to walk through the 6‑week pilot plan?
[00:32] Maya Singh: Sure, quick run. Week 0 is prep, week 1 network+secrets, week 2 staging and bench, week 3 iterations, week 4 canary, week 5 stabilization, week 6 wrap and handoff. Dates flexible of course.
[00:48] Carlos Mendes: Sorry to interrupt, when you say week 1 network, do you need us to open specific ports or are we doing peering? We usually prefer VPC peering.
[00:56] Daniel Wu: Ideally VPC peering — that's simpler for traffic and we can avoid public endpoints. We'll need the CIDR ranges and a window to test, and we'll provide a small NAT instance if needed.
[01:12] Priya Kapoor: Also note, our security policy requires KMS integration — keys must be customer managed and we need proof of zero‑access logs for Redwood.
[01:20] Ethan Park: Totally — we have a KMS flow in our private deployments and Redwood Private supports customer‑managed KMS and HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack that outlines the audit log flows.
[01:31] Renee Lopez: Can you send the SOC2 and pen test artifacts? Our compliance team will want them before we start network peering.
[01:38] Maya Singh: Yes, included in the security pack link I mentioned — there is a SOC2 summary, pen test blurb, and FAQ, but we'll also attach the full reports to your ticket for archival.
[01:50] Samir Patel: Great. On the eval side, Renee, what datasets are you planning to use for the latency tests? Real user payload or synthetic?
[01:57] Renee Lopez: We'll provide a scrubbed sample of our top 500 queries and also a synthetic load generator to hit tails.
[02:05] Daniel Wu: That works. For benchmarking we'll capture p95 and p99 latencies, token costs and throughput. We'll also demonstrate batch sizing and cache behavior — though I may say cache, the transcriber sometimes writes KV cash — which is fine.
[02:23] Carlos Mendes: Ha yeah KV cash.
[02:26] Ethan Park: We should also call out the tradeoffs: we can tune batching to reduce cost but it can increase tail latency. We'll capture tradeoff curves in the bench spreadsheet.
[02:36] Priya Kapoor: On logging — we need access to detailed audit logs for each request and tokenization breakdown — does Redwood provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console?
[02:45] Maya Singh: Yes, per-route/model dashboards include token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and we can grant RBAC to your security account. We'll demo that in the staging walkthrough.
[02:58] Renee Lopez: Awesome. Can we get a sample of the runbook? I want to see the exact steps for failover and rollback.
[03:04] Ethan Park: Yep, I'll share the onboarding runbook after this call. It has a canary run checklist, rollback playbook, alert thresholds, and the exact curl commands for canary traffic.
[03:16] Samir Patel: About the SLA — if we do dedicated capacity later, how fast can Redwood scale? We have seasonal spikes.
[03:24] Daniel Wu: For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools and autoscaling config; burst capacity can be configured. We can model spike scenarios, but the pilot will help us recommend the right pool size.
[03:36] Carlos Mendes: Who from Redwood do we ping for infra issues during the window?
[03:40] Maya Singh: I'll be your primary CSM contact; Daniel will be the SE pager for technical triage; Ethan handles commercial questions. We'll provide a dedicated Slack channel for the pilot.
[03:52] Renee Lopez: Perfect.
[03:55] Ethan Park: Quick note on data residency — you mentioned most workloads are in us‑west, correct?
[03:59] Renee Lopez: Yes, primary is us‑west, but legal asks about euro data for a subset. We'll surface that if/when we expand.
[04:08] Daniel Wu: We can pin model variants by region and route EU traffic to EU regions — it's part of the deployment abstraction.
[04:15] Priya Kapoor: Also SSO — we use Okta. Integration steps?
[04:19] Maya Singh: SAML/SSO via Okta is standard, we'll share SAML metadata and a short guide. You can create an IdP in the console, and we support SCIM for provisioning.
[04:31] Samir Patel: Any known gotchas from previous pilots we should be aware of?
[04:35] Daniel Wu: Two things: 1) Mismatched MTU settings can cause packet drops on peering — ask infra to check. 2) Long prompt context sizes can drive memory and change kernel selection; we'll recommend a quantization profile if you care about cost.
[04:50] Renee Lopez: Good to know.
[04:53] Carlos Mendes: MTU, yes we saw that once.
[04:56] Ethan Park: Ok let's run through the immediate ask list so it's clear. Carlos, you confirm VPC peering CIDRs and firewall rule by 8/31. Priya, send KMS details and initial compliance docs by 9/1. Renee, sample dataset by 9/4. Daniel will get a draft bench plan by 9/6. Ethan will send runbook and links by EOD. Does that timeline work?
[05:20] Renee Lopez: Sounds good.
[05:22] Priya Kapoor: Yes.
[05:24] Samir Patel: One more thing — pricing for the pilot: can you send the pricing sheet and an estimate for 6 weeks?
[05:30] Maya Singh: We'll share an estimate — it's usage-based for hosted during pilot; if you opt for Dedicated we can model reserved commits. We'll attach an example cost model in the sheet.
[05:40] Carlos Mendes: For the bench, can we test both streaming and non-streaming inference modes? We use streaming for token feedback.
[05:47] Daniel Wu: Absolutely — we'll include streaming traces and highlight latency differences.
[05:51] Ethan Park: Ok final quick items: we'll set up the pilot Slack, share the runbook and bench sheet, and schedule the week-2 SE deep-dive for 90 minutes. I'll put tentative invites. Any blockers?
[06:03] Renee Lopez: None on our side, just need the docs to pass compliance.
[06:07] Priya Kapoor: We'll review SOC2 and confirm.
[06:09] Ethan Park: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and the action item list.

Notes about transcription: speaker labels occasionally conflated; timestamps approximate. Some product names transcribed oddly (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache").
